key_evidence: Human Rights Watch reported on 16 July 2026 that since mid-June 2026 security forces have unlawfully seized at least five critics of President Yoweri Museveni and his son, UPDF chief General Muhoozi Kainerugaba.

Since 28 June the military has surrounded and laid siege to Nation Media Group, Uganda’s largest independent media company, after Kainerugaba ordered the shutdown of its television and newspaper operations.

Lawyer Erias Lukwago was seized from his Kampala home on 15 June, the day he prepared to serve legal summons on Kainerugaba. Kainerugaba appeared to confirm holding him and shared a photograph of what appeared to be Lukwago blindfolded.

The UN Secretary-General issued a Note to Correspondents on 2 July 2026 noting concern about detentions of political and civic actors, including cases where whereabouts had not been clearly established. This is tier 5 but is dated outside the 12-26 July window.

Uganda’s prior assessment of 2026-07-12 was a screening confirmation on Marburg and Ebola containment. It explicitly recorded governance concerns as already priced and did not evaluate the June-July seizures, which were first documented publicly on 16 July.

evidence.quote: President Museveni’s government is increasingly using the military as a cudgel against dissent and criticism
evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch characterises the pattern as systematic use of the military against dissent
evidence.source: Carine Kaneza Nantulya, deputy Africa director, Human Rights Watch

evidence.quote: No military officer should be able to carry out serious violations with impunity
evidence.claim: impunity for military officers is the central accountability failure identified
evidence.source: Carine Kaneza Nantulya, Human Rights Watch

evidence.claim: The UN Secretary-General noted with concern reports of detention of political and civic actors in Uganda, including cases in which the whereabouts of some individuals have not been clearly established
evidence.source: United Nations, Spokesman for the Secretary-General

evidence.claim: A rights group condemned the abduction of government critics by the Ugandan military

notes: ROUTED AS FLAG-FOR-REVIEW, NOT AS AN ASSERTED DOWNGRADE. The move crosses a band label: published band developing at 20.3 against an assessed Critical at 13.1. The band-crossing bar requires at least two distinct sources with at least one at sourceTier 4 or above. The strongest in-window source is Human Rights Watch at tier 3; the tier-5 UN Secretary-General note is dated 2 July 2026 and falls outside the 12-26 July window. Human judgment is requested on whether an out-of-window tier-5 corroboration of the same pattern satisfies the bar. BASELINE-PROVENANCE CHECK PERFORMED: research/assessments/uganda-2026-07-12.md is a screening confirmation covering disease containment only; it states that own-conduct governance concerns are already priced and unchanged, and it did not evaluate the June-July military seizures, which were first documented publicly four days later. No stale-baseline rationale is asserted against a documented recent full assessment. DIRECTIONALITY CHECK: negative in-window evidence produces a negative proposal, as required. NOTE ON THE PUBLISHED BAND LABEL: 20.3 is strictly Critical under the 0-20 / 21-40 banding but is labelled developing in the index. This is a pre-existing labelling quirk shared with Honduras and Papua New Guinea and is not created by this proposal.
